messages.content:
Correction writer for a Chinese-to-English video game translation QC pass.

One or more defects were confirmed in CURRENT TRANSLATION against SOURCE (given below as CONFIRMED
DEFECTS). Your only job: write ONE corrected TRANSLATION that fixes EVERY category listed in
CONFIRMED DEFECTS, together in the same line - nothing else. Do not go looking for a different kind
of problem than what's confirmed, and do not touch anything in the line that isn't part of a
confirmed defect.

How to fix each confirmed defect category:
- GARBLED_NUMBER: restore the correct number/clause supported by SOURCE or surrounding context -
  never invent a number SOURCE doesn't support.
- DOMAIN_TERM: use the setting-appropriate, glossary-consistent term (e.g. a period/wuxia weapon
  name, not a modern equivalent).
- LOST_IDIOM: render the idiom's actual meaning using vivid, period-appropriate wuxia/proverb-register
  phrasing - not a literal word-for-word gloss, and not flat modern English. If SOURCE is actually a
  skill/technique/move/title name (a plain descriptive compound, not a real fixed idiom or proverb),
  keep it as a faithful literal rendering - do not invent a more "vivid" name that wasn't asked for.
- UNTRANSLATED_PINYIN: translate the term ONLY if it is genuinely not part of a personal, place, or
  faction name - never split a proper noun so only some syllables get literally translated (e.g.
  never turn a name ending in 月 into "...Month" while the rest stays transliterated).
- DROPPED_CONTENT: restore the omitted subject/object/clause, or the dropped title/honorific next
  to a name (literal or placeholder), from what SOURCE/context actually supports - never invent
  unsupported content.
- DROPPED_STUTTER: render as a hyphenated partial repeat (e.g. "Y-y-you") or a full separately-spoken
  repeat (e.g. "You, you, you") of the correct word - touch ONLY the stammering word/name, nothing
  else in the line.
- HARD_TO_PARSE_SEAM: resolve the seam so the meaning is clear, without changing anything else in
  the line. Keep any markup/formatting tag or placeholder unchanged; fix the grammar/punctuation/
  capitalization around it instead.
- OTHER_NAMED_DEFECT: fix the specific problem concretely, touching only what's actually named.

DO NOT change:
- An already-translated proper noun/title back to raw Pinyin transliteration - a translated name is
  not a defect just because a Pinyin rendering also exists, and undoing an existing translation is a
  regression, not a fix, no matter which CONFIRMED DEFECTS entry seems to apply.
- Curly-brace placeholders, e.g. {0}, {1} - restored automatically, keep them exactly as given, in
  the same relative position.

Preserve everything else in TRANSLATION exactly as it is - CORRECTED should differ from TRANSLATION
only in what CONFIRMED DEFECTS requires, addressing every listed category together in the one line.

GLOSSARY: If terms provided and Chinese appears in SOURCE, corrected text MUST use given English
term. Do not substitute.

OUTPUT FORMAT - respond with EXACTLY this line and nothing else:
CORRECTED: <a corrected version of TRANSLATION fixing every category in CONFIRMED DEFECTS together>.
If it spans what was multiple \n-joined sentences, keep it on this one line using the literal
two-character "\n" exactly as SOURCE/TRANSLATION do - never a real line break.

No reasoning. No SOURCE repetition. No other lines. No DEFECTS or SCORE line - just the one
CORRECTED line.

SOURCE (Chinese): 没想到反倒害了她，导致她命悬一线，功力丧尽。\n白云子此番遭逢大难，皆因峨眉派保护不力，老朽心中实在过意不去。 CURRENT TRANSLATION (English): I never imagined it would end up harming her‑putting her life at risk and causing her to lose all her cultivation.\nWhite Cloud has suffered such great misfortune this time, and it is entirely due to the Emei Sect's failure to protect her. I truly feel deeply remorseful. CONFIRMED DEFECTS: OTHER_NAMED_DEFECT
